title: Do concept probes beat an LLM judge for diffuse safety categories?

original_idea.body: Train linear probes for 3 diffuse safety categories and compare against a same-size LLM-judge to see where probes win for fuzzy-reward categories.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Probes-beat-judges for fuzzy categories (manipulation, deception, power-seeking) targets a recognized hard monitoring pathway.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Probe training + LLM-judge comparison is accessible, but labeling fuzzy categories with reliable ground truth is harder.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable but constructing labeled sets for 3 fuzzy categories adds a data-curation dependency.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Fuzzy-reward safety monitoring is exactly the neglected, hard-to-automate area labs deprioritize; no internal access.

low_compute.reasoning: Inference + tiny probe training on one model; single GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Probes-beat-judges shown for hallucination/toxicity; the diffuse-category extension is a partly-open follow-up.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Probes-beat-judges is shown for some categories; whether it holds for diffuse/fuzzy categories is a partly-open extension.
